title: Cortical Interneurons
intro: GABAergic interneurons make up roughly a fifth of cortical neurons but most of its diversity. They release GABA, inhibit their targets, and with few exceptions keep their axons inside the local circuit. Each type inhibits a particular part of its targets (the soma, the axon, the dendrites or other interneurons) at a particular time, and that division of labour is what lets a column control the timing, gain and routing of its excitatory activity.

blocks.text: Three families cover almost all of them

Cortical interneurons are born outside the cortex, in the ganglionic eminences of the embryonic brain, and migrate in. Their developmental origin sorts them into three non-overlapping molecular families that together account for nearly all cortical GABAergic cells in mouse (Rudy et al. 2011): parvalbumin (PV, about 40 per cent), somatostatin (SST, about 30 per cent), both from the medial ganglionic eminence, and the 5HT3a-receptor family (about 30 per cent), from the caudal ganglionic eminence, which includes VIP cells and most neurogliaform cells. Transcriptomics splits each family into many subtypes (Tasic et al. 2018), but these three remain the backbone.

items: Output control (PV): basket and chandelier cells inhibit near the spike initiation zone, so they decide whether and when a pyramidal cell fires. They are recruited first by both feedforward and feedback excitation.

Input control (SST): Martinotti cells inhibit dendrites, so they decide which inputs, especially top-down ones in layer 1, are integrated. They are recruited by sustained activity through facilitating synapses.

Inhibition of inhibition (VIP): VIP cells inhibit SST cells and thereby release pyramidal dendrites. Long-range and neuromodulatory inputs engage them, so they open the gate under attention, locomotion or reward.

Slow, wide inhibition (neurogliaform): neurogliaform cells release GABA into the space around their dense axons and produce slow GABA-B inhibition of everything nearby, including the tufts of pyramidal cells in layer 1.

blocks.text: Pfeffer et al. (2013) mapped the connections among PV, SST and VIP cells in mouse V1 and found a clear motif: PV cells inhibit each other and pyramidal cells; SST cells inhibit everyone except other SST cells; VIP cells mainly inhibit SST cells. This motif is the basis of most circuit models of cortical inhibition, for example the disinhibitory gain model of Fu et al. (2014) and the stabilised-supralinear network models of Litwin-Kumar et al. (2016) and Garcia del Molino et al. (2017).

items: Point neurons per family are standard: fast-spiking for PV (Izhikevich FS, or a Wang-Buzsaki conductance model), low-threshold spiking for SST, adapting or irregular spiking for VIP.
Give each family its own synaptic dynamics: depressing excitation onto PV, facilitating onto SST, and slow GABA-B output from neurogliaform cells.
Give each family its own target compartment if your excitatory cells have dendrites: PV onto the soma, SST onto the apical compartment.

Detailed models: Blue Brain's 11 interneuron m-types per layer (large, nest and small basket cells, chandelier, Martinotti, bipolar, double bouquet, bitufted, neurogliaform and others) with fitted e-types; the Allen Institute's interneuron GLIF and all-active models; Hippocampome.org's hippocampal interneuron parameter sets.
